THE ACCELERATION LOOP

Research → engineer → research the issues → engineer to completion.

The harness creates an integrated first-pass concept package in hours. It does not compress physical testing, qualification, certification, or mission acceptance into hours.

01

Research

Synthesize sources, rank hypotheses, expose uncertainty, and define discriminating measurements.

02

Engineer

Translate validated knowledge into requirements, interfaces, trades, analyses, and verification plans.

03

Research issues

Return conflicts, missing evidence, failed assumptions, and unresolved risks to targeted inquiry.

04

Engineer to completion

Revise the configuration, close requirements, execute verification, and preserve the decision record.

Harness advantage

Specialists share typed work products, provenance, memory, and promotion gates. Each cycle starts with the best validated state instead of rebuilding context.

PROCESS EVOLUTION

Specialists in sequence. Evidence at every handoff.

The harness progresses only when a typed work product satisfies its promotion contract.

HYPATIA + HYPERIA

Discover what is true—and what is still unknown.

Rank hypotheses, synthesize sources, and label every consequential claim as Observed, Derived, Assumed, or Unknown.

RECURSIVE SPECIALIST ORGANIZATION

Three domain leads. Thirty-one core specialists. More depth on demand.

The Mission Harness Director assigns work to domain leads. Each lead may spawn bounded specialist agents—and those agents may spawn narrower experts—without expanding authority or escaping evidence, cost, depth, and approval limits.

HUMAN MISSION AUTHORITY→MISSION HARNESS DIRECTOR→SCIENCE • ENGINEERING • PROGRAM
SCIENCE DOMAIN

Science Domain Lead

Owns the question, evidence plan, hypotheses, experiments, uncertainty, review, and Engineering Evidence Package.

  • Research question + scope
  • Literature + source intelligence
  • Hypothesis + causal model
  • Experiment design
  • Simulation + scientific modeling
  • Data stewardship + statistics
  • Scientific visualization
  • Independent scientific review
  • Science synthesis + handoff
May add geology, atmosphere, materials, radiation, biology, instrumentation, or replication experts.
ENGINEERING DOMAIN

Engineering Domain Lead

Owns the controlled technical baseline from ConOps through verification, release, manufacturing, and operations readiness.

  • ConOps + stakeholder needs
  • Requirements + traceability
  • Architecture + interfaces
  • Trade + decision analysis
  • Discipline coordination
  • Modeling + digital twin
  • Safety, reliability + FMEA
  • Verification + validation
  • Manufacturing + integration
  • Configuration + release
  • Independent design review
May add mechanical, electrical, software, controls, thermal, structures, power, communications, human-factors, or ISRU experts.
PROJECT MANAGEMENT DOMAIN

Program Domain Lead

Owns authorized scope, integrated execution, performance measurement, governance, change, and closeout.

  • Charter, scope + governance
  • WBS + deliverables
  • Schedule + critical path
  • Resources + capacity
  • Cost + earned value
  • Risk + opportunity
  • Quality + acceptance
  • Change coordination
  • Communications + status
  • Procurement + partners
  • Closure + lessons
Coordinates domain work but cannot approve scientific truth, technical adequacy, or safety risk.
EVERY SPAWN IS A CONTRACT

Bound the work before multiplying the workers.

  1. Define task, parent, scope, exclusions, evidence, and output.
  2. Limit tools, time, cost, child count, depth, and authority.
  3. Execute in parallel with shared memory and typed handoffs.
  4. Review independently; no agent approves its own consequential work.
  5. Promote, return, block, or escalate through the domain lead.

GROUND-TRUTH CASE / SCALED MOXIE

Proof is not permission to overclaim.

What this case study tests: NASA’s MOXIE demonstrated that oxygen can be produced from the Martian atmosphere at gram scale. This case study asks what it would take to scale that achievement into a complete oxygen system producing many tonnes: enough life-support oxygen for a 12-person habitat over two years, plus the liquid-oxygen oxidizer needed to refuel a spacecraft for its return to Earth. MOXIE’s results are observed evidence; the large-scale mission target and plant design are modeled concepts that still require engineering validation.

NASA reports 16 oxygen-producing runs, 122 g total output, a peak of 12 g/h, and oxygen purity of at least 98%. These are observed demonstration facts. The crew-scale concept uses solid-oxide carbon-dioxide electrolysis, but its scale-up values remain modeled outputs—not flight-qualified performance.

OBSERVED16 runs • 122 g • 12 g/h • ≥98%PASS
MODELED304 kWe • 592 t • 585 t • 7.4 t • 33.8 kg/hTRACE
UNKNOWNCrew-scale reliability, qualification, and flight readinessBLOCK

Scenario figures require the calculation references and assumptions documented in the case-study and claims-ledger files.

FIFTEEN PRACTICAL CONCLUSIONS

What changes for science, engineering, and project execution.

SCIENCE
  1. Keep evidence classes explicit.
  2. Use competing hypotheses, not one favored story.
  3. Design measurements that discriminate.
  4. Carry uncertainty into engineering.
  5. Make negative results reusable mission memory.
ENGINEERING
  1. Translate evidence into traceable requirements.
  2. Keep assumptions and interfaces configuration-controlled.
  3. Recompute consequential values independently.
  4. Return unresolved issues to targeted research.
  5. Close with verification evidence, not confidence alone.
PROJECT MANAGEMENT
  1. Promote work only through explicit gates.
  2. Assign owners, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
  3. Separate rapid concept generation from qualification.
  4. Make rollback and escalation normal controls.
  5. Measure outcomes and version the process.
